definition: To live in a particular place
example_sentence: Most of the workers reside near the factory.

definition: To calculate a number or amount, especially with a machine
example_sentence: The program computes the average score automatically.

definition: An official group given a task, or money paid for selling something
example_sentence: A special commission investigated the accident.

definition: An official plan for doing something, or a secret plan
example_sentence: The government launched a scheme to help small businesses.

definition: Relating to a large company
example_sentence: Corporate profits rose sharply last year.

definition: To think that something is probably true, often something bad
example_sentence: Police suspect that the fire was started on purpose.

definition: To have enough money or time for something
example_sentence: Many young families cannot afford to buy a home.

definition: To tell people something officially
example_sentence: The university announced a new scholarship program.

definition: To officially accept a plan or request, or to think something is good
example_sentence: The committee approved the new budget.

definition: To try to do something, especially something difficult
example_sentence: Several companies attempted to enter the market.

definition: To say that someone or something is responsible for something bad
example_sentence: Many people blame social media for rising anxiety.

definition: To decide that a planned event will not happen
example_sentence: The flight was canceled because of the storm.

definition: To say that you are unhappy or not satisfied with something
example_sentence: Residents complained about the noise from the airport.

definition: To state something officially or firmly
example_sentence: The government declared a state of emergency.

definition: To protect someone or something from attack or criticism
example_sentence: The author defended her theory against its critics.

definition: To make something happen later than planned
example_sentence: Heavy rain delayed the start of the project.

definition: To have earned something because of your actions or qualities
example_sentence: Nurses deserve better working conditions.

definition: To pay no attention to something or someone
example_sentence: Many drivers ignore the speed limit.

definition: To say firmly that something must happen or is true
example_sentence: The manager insisted on checking every report.

definition: To make someone agree or do something by giving reasons
example_sentence: The campaign persuaded many people to stop smoking.

definition: To make someone suffer for doing something wrong
example_sentence: Students who cheat are punished severely.

definition: To feel sorry about something you did or did not do
example_sentence: Many people regret not studying harder at school.

definition: To save someone from a dangerous situation
example_sentence: Firefighters rescued a family from the burning building.

definition: To end an argument, or to go and live in a new place
example_sentence: The two sides finally settled the dispute.

definition: To try very hard to do something difficult
example_sentence: Many small businesses struggle to survive.

definition: A person in your family who lived long before you
example_sentence: Our ancestors lived by hunting and gathering.

definition: A feeling of worry about what may happen
example_sentence: Exams cause anxiety in many students.

definition: Something difficult or unpleasant that you have to deal with
example_sentence: High taxes are a heavy burden on the poor.

definition: Belief in your own abilities, or trust in someone or something
example_sentence: Public confidence in the banks fell during the crisis.

definition: A way of behaving that is usual in a society
example_sentence: The custom of giving gifts is common in many cultures.

definition: A sudden event that causes great damage or loss of life
example_sentence: The flood was the worst natural disaster in decades.

definition: A large amount of water covering land that is usually dry
example_sentence: The flood destroyed hundreds of homes.

definition: Physical or mental damage
example_sentence: The chemicals can cause serious harm to fish.

definition: A natural way of behaving that is not learned
example_sentence: Birds build nests by instinct.

definition: Strong support for a person, group or idea
example_sentence: Companies reward customer loyalty with discounts.

definition: What you think or believe about something
example_sentence: Public opinion on the issue is divided.

definition: A situation in which there is not enough of something
example_sentence: The region faces a serious water shortage.

definition: A person who is harmed or killed by a crime, accident or disease
example_sentence: The victims of the earthquake received emergency aid.

definition: Money paid for work, usually by the hour or week
example_sentence: The minimum wage rose by five percent.

definition: Willing to face danger or pain without showing fear
example_sentence: The brave soldier saved his friends.

definition: Wanting to know or learn about something
example_sentence: Young children are naturally curious about the world.

definition: Wanting very much to do or have something
example_sentence: The students were eager to see their results.

definition: Willing to give more money, time or help than expected
example_sentence: The museum received a generous donation.

definition: Telling the truth and not cheating
example_sentence: Most people believe they are more honest than others.

definition: Not guilty of a crime, or not knowing about bad things
example_sentence: The court found the man innocent.

definition: Very serious or bad
example_sentence: The region suffered a severe drought last summer.

definition: Right or acceptable for a particular purpose
example_sentence: The land is not suitable for farming.

definition: Needing attention immediately
example_sentence: The hospital made an urgent call for blood donors.

definition: Only; used to say something is not more important than it seems
example_sentence: The report merely describes the problem without solving it.

definition: Approximately, or in a rough way
example_sentence: Roughly half of the population lives in cities.

definition: A little
example_sentence: Prices rose slightly in the first quarter.

definition: Because something might happen
example_sentence: Take an umbrella in case it rains.

definition: Until now
example_sentence: So far, no one has found a cure for the disease.
